
The task page shows the header card (identity, state, priority, kind, project, lease holder) and then the body. Every other section follows as a native `<details>` element, collapsed by default, with its heading and, where cheap, a count as the summary: Prerequisites, Agent sessions, Activity, Attachments, Edges, Timeline. Prerequisites draws `store.BlockerTree` (the same rows as `GET /api/v1/tasks/{id}/blockers`) top-down: the task at the top and its direct prerequisites below it as a wrapping row of cards, so nothing scrolls sideways. Each card shows its linked id, title and state, and a card with prerequisites of its own says how many levels and distinct open tasks sit beneath it ("3 levels · 7 tasks below"). It is a native `<details>`: opening it shows its next level only. Each task is drawn in full once, at its shallowest position. Every later occurrence is a compact reference that links to that card, and the edge that closes a cycle is a reference marked cycle. The root's blocking plans have their own cards, and a full-title list is the accessible form. The summary counts the open prerequisites and the direct ones and names the frontier as candidates, never as claimable. A cycle, or a tree cut at its card cap, is stated on the page. The section is omitted when nothing holds the task.
